22.5 Petrochemicals

Petroleum is a complex mixture of hydrocarbons formed by the decomposition of fossil remains. It exists as a gas (natural gas), liquid (crude oil) or as solids (oil shales) and is found deep underground or below seabed. About 10% of the petroleum is used to prepare a range of chemicals called petrochemicals. Petrochemicals as a group of chemicals produced directly or indirectly from the hydrocarbons of petroleum or natural gas. Examples of petrochemicals are plastics, rubbers, fibres, paints, solvents, and detergents.

Since every area of human activity makes use of petrochemicals or the materials made from them, our life without petrochemicals would be very different and less comfortable. The different petrochemicals are compiled in Table 22.2.

Table 22.2 Some Important Petrochemicals

The Basic Building Block Processes

The basic building block petrochemical processes are divided into two groups. These processes are cracking and reforming process.

i. Cracking Process

Cracking is a process in which molecules of raw material are dissociated into smaller ones. There are two types of cracking process, thermal steam cracking and catalytic cracking.

a. Thermal Steam Cracking

Steam cracking is the breaking of raw material such as ethane and propane yielding important petrochemical products, such as ethene and propene. Methane and hydrogen are also some of the major by-products.

b. Catalytic Cracking

Breaking of larger, stable molecules requires catalysis. Refinery products such as gas oil and fuel oil is passed through catalytic cracker to obtain gasoline and kerosene oil as major products and by-product, propene.

22.5 Petrochemicals

Petroleum is a complex mixture of hydrocarbons formed by the decomposition of fossil remains. It exists as a gas (natural gas), liquid (crude oil) or as solids (oil shales) and is found deep underground or below seabed. About 10% of the petroleum is used to prepare a range of chemicals called petrochemicals. Petrochemicals as a group of chemicals produced directly or indirectly from the hydrocarbons of petroleum or natural gas. Examples of petrochemicals are plastics, rubbers, fibres, paints, solvents, and detergents.

Since every area of human activity makes use of petrochemicals or the materials made from them, our life without petrochemicals would be very different and less comfortable. The different petrochemicals are compiled in Table 22.2.

Table 22.2 Some Important Petrochemicals

The Basic Building Block Processes

The basic building block petrochemical processes are divided into two groups. These processes are cracking and reforming process.

i. Cracking Process

Cracking is a process in which molecules of raw material are dissociated into smaller ones. There are two types of cracking process, thermal steam cracking and catalytic cracking.

a. Thermal Steam Cracking

Steam cracking is the breaking of raw material such as ethane and propane yielding important petrochemical products, such as ethene and propene. Methane and hydrogen are also some of the major by-products.

b. Catalytic Cracking

Breaking of larger, stable molecules requires catalysis. Refinery products such as gas oil and fuel oil is passed through catalytic cracker to obtain gasoline and kerosene oil as major products and by-product, propene.
